overview.title: CodeOwl Help Center
overview.lead: Everything you need to know about CodeOwl v2 — generating, reviewing, and solving tiered Parsons problems in a classroom context.
overview.authBody: CodeOwl v2 has full user accounts with three roles: Teacher, Student, and Admin. Teachers self-register; students are enrolled by their teacher via a one-time token link (no email required on day one).
authItems: Login — Email + password, or token link (for students).
Register — Teachers only. Students are created by the teacher.
Onboarding — Students set their own password after first login.
Profile — Change email or password at any time.
overview.homeBody: The starting point for creating tiered Parsons problem sets. Provide code, a problem statement, and/or concepts. CodeOwl generates three (or five) task tiers automatically.
homeItems: Generate Sequence — creates a new 3-tier (or 5-tier) Parsons problem set.
Target Language — force problem statements in German or English.
Demo / Reset — load a sample or clear the form.
overview.manualBody: No LLM involved — write your own problem statements and code solutions directly. Ideal when you want full control over the exact wording and code, or when you already have classroom examples you want to turn into Parsons puzzles.
manualItems: Tier Editor — write up to 3 tiers (T1–T3); each tier gets its own statement and code.
Live Block Preview — see how the code will be split into draggable blocks as you type.
Tab key — inserts 4 spaces in the code editor (no focus-trap).
overview.classesBody: Teachers create classes, manage student accounts within them, and assign worksheets. Students are enrolled via a generated token link — no email required at sign-up.
classesItems: Create Class — name your class and add students.
Student Tokens — one-time login links for each student.
Assign Worksheets — attach worksheets to a class so students can access them.
Tracking — enable per-class tracking to log detailed learning events for research.
overview.myClassesBody: Students see their assigned classes and worksheets here. Each class card links to the worksheets the teacher has assigned — click a worksheet to start solving tasks.
myClassesItems: Click a class card to see its worksheets.
Click a worksheet to open it and see all tasks.
If your class list is empty, ask your teacher to enrol you.
overview.worksheetsBody: Worksheets group sequences into a coherent unit (e.g., "Week 3 — Arrays"). Teachers assign worksheets to classes, configure hint settings, and export them to PDF.
worksheetsItems: Manage Sequences — add or remove sequences from a worksheet.
Hint Configuration — enable/disable hints, set credits per task.
Assign to Class — make the worksheet visible to students.
Export — PDF (puzzle or free-form) and CSV/JSON export.
overview.libraryBody: Browse, search, and reuse all sequences available to you. Filter by programming language, concept tags, tier count, or full-text search. Copy any sequence into your own worksheet with one click.
libraryItems: Full-Text Search — searches problem statements and code simultaneously.
One-Click Copy — copy a sequence directly into one of your worksheets.
overview.curriculumBody: Browse the Bavarian LehrplanPLUS (G9 Informatik) topic tree and generate sequences directly from a curriculum topic. CodeOwl automatically fills in concepts and injects curated reference code for the chosen grade level.
curriculumItems: Auto-Context — concepts and code examples pre-filled from the topic.
Grade Calibration — the prompt adapts difficulty to the selected grade.
overview.marketplaceBody: Browse whole worksheets other teachers have published, not just individual sequences. Copy any published worksheet into your own space with one click.
marketplaceItems: Search & Sort — by name/description, recency, relevance, or popularity.
Copy Worksheet — deep-copies the whole worksheet, every sequence and task inside it.
Publishing — set a worksheet's visibility to "In the marketplace" to list it here.
overview.sequenceBody: Overview of all tasks (T1–T3 or T1–T5) within a generated sequence. Teachers see model solutions, can edit tasks, and export the sequence.
sequenceItems: Solve Task / Review Task — student or teacher solver view.
Edit Task — adjust problem statement and code (teacher only).
Share Sequence — copies a student-safe link to clipboard.
overview.solveBody: The interactive Parsons problem solver. Drag, click, or use keyboard to arrange shuffled code blocks, then request feedback.
solveItems: Check my solution — green / yellow / red per block.
Distractors — plausible but incorrect blocks that must be identified and excluded.
Hints — static-analysis-powered hints that highlight problematic blocks.
Completion Banner — "Solved correctly!" with stats when correct.
overview.hintsBody: When a student is stuck, the hint system runs static analysis on the current block arrangement and highlights the problematic blocks — no guesswork, no hallucination. A second tier optionally calls the LLM for a student-friendly explanation.
hintsItems: Level 1 — deterministic: Ruff (Python) or javac/SpotBugs (Java) identifies the error.
Level 2 — "Explain it to me": the LLM explains the finding in plain language.
overview.distractorsBody: Distractor blocks are plausible-looking but incorrect code lines mixed into the puzzle pool. Students must identify and exclude them. Taxonomy-based (6 types), LLM-generated by a separate "Antagonist" call.
distractorsItems: Types — Logic Flip, Off-by-One, Variable Mismatch, Boundary Identity, Structural Illogical, Redundant Zombie.
Teacher Controls — edit, regenerate, or disable distractors per task.
Hint Integration — hints detect distractor blocks first before doing full analysis.
overview.teacherBody: Teachers and admins automatically have access to Teacher Mode — model solutions, review tools, edit controls, and export options.
teacherItems: Toggle the "Teacher View" button to reveal/hide model solutions.
Edit tasks, manage distractors, configure hints per worksheet.
Students never see teacher controls regardless of URL.
overview.adminBody: Admin-only tools for managing the platform: user accounts, tag hygiene, and bulk operations on library content.
adminItems: User Management — view, edit roles, and delete user accounts.
Library Admin — merge duplicate tags, bulk-retag sequences after model updates.

auth.title: Accounts & Authentication
auth.intro: CodeOwl v2 has full user accounts with three roles. All learning data (events, feedback logs) is linked to a user ID where available. Anonymous visitors can still open shared links and solve tasks, but they cannot generate or create anything — the start page is the login page.
roles: Teacher — can generate sequences (the Home Page is only available to teachers and admins), manage classes, create/edit worksheets.
Student — can solve tasks in assigned worksheets; cannot generate.
Admin — all teacher permissions plus user management and admin tools.
registration: Register — teachers self-register with name, email, and password. Email verification is sent automatically.
Login — email + password (teachers/admins), or a one-time token link (students).
Token Login — students paste or click the link generated by their teacher. No email required to start.

FIM / University Login — at institutions with a matching LDAP directory, "Login with FIM-Account" lets a teacher sign in with their existing university credentials, and lets students created that way do the same instead of using a token link.
auth.onboarding: Students do not self-register. The teacher creates student accounts inside a class. CodeOwl generates a personal token link per student — share this link (printed, chat, etc.). The student clicks it, is logged in immediately, and can optionally set an email and password during onboarding. This minimises friction on day one.
password: Forgot Password — enter your email to receive a reset link.
Reset Password — follow the link in the email to set a new password.
Profile — change email address or password at any time via your profile page.
security: Passwords are hashed with Argon2 — they are never stored in plain text.
JWTs expire and auto-refresh in the background.
Student token links are single-use; once redeemed they cannot be reused.

home.title: Home Page Help
home.intro: The Home Page is your workspace for generating new tiered programming tasks. CodeOwl accepts multiple types of input and creates three tasks (T1–T3) — or five tasks (T1–T5) in extended mode.
inputs: Code Snippet — paste a valid snippet; the model creates statements and variants.
Problem Statement — describe the problem in plain language.
Concepts — list programming ideas like loops, arrays, or recursion.
Important! — Either a Code Snippet must be present or the language must be explicitly stated. Context can be derived from everything except the language alone.
options: Target Language — forces problem statements and code comments to be in German or English. Fixes the v1 problem where generation silently switched languages.
Tier Count — 3 tiers (default) or 5 tiers. Tier 4 adds distractor-heavy puzzles; Tier 5 adds an "Explain Your Solution" component.
Distractors — enable or disable LLM-generated distractor blocks. When enabled, a separate "Antagonist" call generates plausible-but-wrong lines per task.
home.contextModeBody: wraps the puzzle in read-only scaffolding code. The generated task receives a contextBefore and contextAfter block (e.g. a class header above and a calling function below). Students see the full picture but only rearrange the puzzle blocks in the middle. Useful for longer, realistic code problems.
home.inlineSplitBody: some lines are additionally split into fragments the student must order within the block itself, not just place the block as a whole — useful for lines with several independent sub-expressions.
advanced: Blacklist — comma-separated constructs to exclude, e.g., ternary, lambda, list comprehension. Prevents LLM from using concepts students haven't learned yet.
Whitelist — only use listed constructs. Useful for highly controlled exercises.
Difficulty Slope — controls how steep the complexity jump between tiers is (gentle → steep).
Additional Context — freetext injected directly into the prompt, e.g., "Use only German variable names" or "Suitable for Jgst. 9".
controls: Generate Sequence — sends inputs to the model and redirects to the sequence page.
Create Worksheet — opens a small modal to create an empty worksheet directly from Home, without generating a sequence first.
Demo — instantly loads a sample tiered sequence for testing.
tips: Very short snippets can cause wrong language detection — set the language explicitly.
Use clear, short statements. Avoid specifying variable names or function identifiers.
English input yields slightly better quality than German, but German works reliably with Target Language: German set.
If the generated tasks use constructs students don't know yet, add them to the Blacklist and regenerate.

classes.title: Classes Help
classes.intro: Classes group students together and connect them to worksheets. Every student account belongs to at least one class.
overview: The Classes page lists all your classes with student counts and assigned worksheets.
Click a class to open the detail view: student list + worksheet list.
classes.createBody: Click "Add student" inside a class — enter a display name (first name, e.g., "Anton"). CodeOwl creates the account and shows a one-time login token link. Share this link with the student (print, chat, QR code). The student clicks it, is instantly logged in, and can start solving tasks. No email address is required.
create: Token links can be regenerated if lost.
Students can later add an email and set a password via their profile page.
Students can be removed from a class at any time (this does not delete the account).
"Import CSV" — add a whole class list at once: download the template, fill it in, preview the rows, then create them all in one step.

FIM / University Accounts — "Add FIM-Accounts" adds students by their FIM username (single or bulk via CSV) if your institution's LDAP identity applies; they log in via "Login with FIM-Account" instead of a token link.
"Download invite links (CSV)" — every student's token link as a CSV; "Download unregistered (CSV)" narrows that to the ones who haven't logged in yet.
"Set temporary password" — generates a new temporary password, shown once, for a student who's lost access to their token link and can't recover it themselves.
assign: From the class detail page, click "Assign worksheet" and pick from your worksheets.
Assigned worksheets become accessible to all students in the class.
Worksheets can also be assigned directly from the Worksheet page.
classes.trackingBody: Each class has a Tracking toggle (⚙ button in the class detail view). When enabled, detailed learning events are recorded for every student interaction in this class — block moves, feedback clicks, hint usage, completion times.
tracking: Enabled — full event stream logged; suitable for research or detailed progress analysis.
Disabled — only aggregate data is kept (correct/incorrect per task). Default for new classes.
Tracking state can be toggled at any time; it affects future events only.
progress: When tracking is enabled, the class detail page shows a per-student table — solved-task count, and total/correct attempts.
Click a student to open their detailed progress: every task in every assigned worksheet, with attempt counts and a status (Solved / Attempted / Not attempted).

The "View" button ("Last state" column) on any task opens exactly what the student last had arranged in the solution area — this works even if they never clicked Feedback, since it comes from autosave, not just graded attempts.
permissions: Only the class owner (or admin) can add/remove students or edit the class.
Other teachers can see a class if they share a worksheet with it, but cannot edit it.

worksheets.title: Worksheets Help
worksheets.intro: A worksheet is a named collection of sequences (e.g., "Week 3 — Arrays & Loops"). Worksheets are the primary unit assigned to classes.
overview: Create a worksheet from the Worksheets page or directly from a generated sequence.
Add sequences to a worksheet via the sequence page, the Library (one-click copy), or directly on the Worksheet page — search-and-pick, paste a single sequence ID, or paste several at once.
Sequences within a worksheet preserve their T1–T3 tier structure and can be reordered by drag-and-drop.
A "detail level" toggle (None / Some / All) controls how much per-sequence info the list shows, fetched lazily as you ask for more.
visibility: Only me — nobody else can open this worksheet, not even with a link.
Anyone with the link — whoever has the link can open it; it appears in no search. This was the only option worksheets used to have.
In the marketplace — other teachers can find it by searching (see the Marketplace help page) and copy it into their own space.
Your default "inbox" worksheet can never be published — the option is hidden for it.
worksheets.scheduleBody: Each worksheet assignment to a class can carry its own schedule, edited from the class detail page:
schedule: Released from — when students can start; empty means available at once.
Deadline — after this, students see a closed banner and can view but not edit their work. Empty means open indefinitely.
Grace period — extra hours/minutes tacked on after the deadline before it actually closes; empty or 0 means a sharp cutoff.
Publish now / Unpublish / End now — quick actions that override the schedule immediately, alongside a status badge (Not released yet / Open / Deadline passed).
worksheets.hintsBody: Per worksheet, configure whether hints are available to students and whether their use is capped:
hints: Enable Hints — checkbox on/off. When off, the Hint button doesn't appear.

Unlimited hints — the default. Switch it off to set a budget: Credits per task (1–99). Level-1 hints cost 1 credit, level-2 cost 2. The budget is per student per task and is not refilled when a task is reset.
export: Puzzle PDF — printable cut-and-arrange cards with dashed borders (for paper-based sessions).
Free-Form PDF — problem statement + code in a grey monospace box (for written exams).
JSON / CSV — raw task data for your own analysis (SPSS, R, Excel).
copy: You can view any worksheet shared to you; click "Copy" to get your own editable version.
The deep copy duplicates all sequences and tasks with new IDs — you are the sole owner.
Changes to the copy never affect the original.

library.title: Library Help
library.intro: The Library is a searchable repository of all sequences available to you — your own, plus those shared by colleagues. Find what you need, preview it, and copy it into a worksheet with one click.
search: Full-Text Search — searches problem statements and code simultaneously. Postgres full-text indexing ensures fast, relevant results.
Highlighted Snippets — matching text is highlighted in the result card so you immediately see why a sequence matched.
"Did you mean one of these tags?" — trigram-based fuzzy suggestions for typos (recursiv → recursive).
library.tagsBody: Every sequence has two layers of tags:
tags: Structural Tags (grey) — automatically detected from code: for-loop, recursion, arrays. These are added synchronously right after generation.
Semantic Tags (with ✨) — LLM-generated topic labels: fibonacci, binary-search, caesar-cipher. These arrive a few seconds after generation.
Manual Tags (blue) — added by the teacher; never overwritten by auto-tagging.
library.filtersBody: Filters include: programming language, tier count (3 or 5), tags, date created, owner ("Mine" / "All").
library.filtersUrl: Filters are reflected in the URL so links can be shared.
library.conceptsBody: Alongside tags, sequences are also linked to entries in the curated concept catalogue (the same one used by generation and the curriculum mapping) — a second filter dimension in the sidebar.
concepts: Every sequence card shows the concepts it covers, right next to its tags — click one to filter by it, the same way a tag chip does.
The sidebar's concept cloud works exactly like the tag cloud: a count per concept, "show more", and an any/all match mode once you've picked several.
copy: Click "Copy" on any sequence card to copy it straight into your Library Inbox — a default worksheet CodeOwl keeps for exactly this, no picker involved.
A toast notification confirms the copy with an Undo option (5 seconds).
Sequences already in one of your worksheets show a green ✓ indicator.
addToWorksheet: Click "Add to Worksheet" instead of "Copy" when you want to pick the destination yourself — it opens a modal listing your worksheets.
Unlike "Copy", this doesn't touch your Library Inbox at all.
bulk: Click "Select" above the results grid to turn on a checkbox on every card.
Pick as many sequences as you like, across pages — a sticky bar at the bottom tracks your count.
"Copy N to worksheet" sends them all to one worksheet in a single request and shows how many were added versus already present.
edit: Hover over a tag on your own sequence to reveal the remove (×) button.
Click the pencil icon to add new tags. An autocomplete suggests existing tags to avoid duplicates.
Manual tags are always blue and are never overwritten by the auto-tagger.
library.curriculumBody: From the Curriculum page, “View sequences” redirects to the Library with the curriculum topic pre-filled as a filter — so you instantly see all relevant material for a given topic, whether it is a grade level or a module.

marketplace.title: Marketplace Help
marketplace.intro: The Marketplace is where whole worksheets get published for other teachers to find and reuse — a step up from the Library, which shares individual sequences rather than a full worksheet.
search: Full-Text Search — searches worksheet names and descriptions.
Sort — Recent, Relevance (once you've typed a search), or Popularity.
Language Filter — narrow results to a single programming language.
"Only mine" — show only worksheets you've published yourself, with a count.
copy: Click "Copy" on any card (not shown on your own worksheets) to deep-copy the whole worksheet — every sequence and task inside it — into your own worksheets.
This differs from the Library's one-click copy, which copies a single sequence rather than an entire worksheet.
You're taken straight to your new copy afterwards.
publishing: A worksheet only appears here once its Visibility is set to "In the marketplace" on the Worksheet page — see the Worksheets help page for the other two visibility levels.
Your default "inbox" worksheet can never be published.

curriculum.title: Curriculum Help
curriculum.intro: The Curriculum page maps CodeOwl onto a topic tree: Bavarian grade levels (LehrplanPLUS G9 Informatik) and university modules such as “Programmieren 1”. Browse by entry and learning area, then generate a sequence whose difficulty and concepts are automatically calibrated to that topic — no manual setup needed.
curriculum.betaNote: Beta feature. Curriculum-generated sequences use a dedicated prompt that takes the topic's education level into account — school or university. The underlying code examples are curated by hand and exist for only some topics so far; without one, generation is disabled.
tree: Topics are organised by grade (Jgst. 7, 9, 10, 11, 12/13) and learning area.
Each topic badge shows how many sequences already exist for that topic.
School / University filter — when the tree mixes both, chips at the top let you narrow it to one or the other.
curriculum.generateBody: Click "Generate task" next to a topic. The generation dialog opens pre-filled:
generate: Concepts — automatically set from the curriculum topic mapping.
Code Example — a curated reference code snippet for the topic is injected as seed material.
Language — Java by default (as per Bavarian curriculum); can be changed.
Grade Calibration — the system prompt internally adjusts expected difficulty and prerequisite knowledge.
curriculum.generateAfter: You can modify any pre-filled value before generating, and all standard generation options (constraints, tier count, target language) are available.
curriculum.viewBody: Click "View sequences" next to a topic to jump to the Library pre-filtered for that topic. This includes both curriculum-generated and manually tagged sequences that match.
tips: For Jgst. 7 topics, keep constraints simple — the calibration already limits complexity.
Add your own curated code snippet instead of the default if you have a specific classroom example to use.
After generating, review the output in Teacher Mode before assigning to students.
admin: Grade / Module entries — create or edit top-level entries: a Bavarian grade (with track) or a university module.
Learning-area sub-topics — create or edit sub-topics under an entry, with a name and description in both German and English, and mapped concepts.
Curated code examples — create, edit, or delete the reference snippets a topic offers during generation. A topic with none disables generation for it until one exists.

sequence.title: Sequence Page Help
sequence.intro: The Sequence Page displays all tasks within a generated sequence. Each task corresponds to a tier — Tier 1 is easiest, Tier 3 (or 5) is most complex.
overview: Language / Concepts — detected programming language, concept tags, semantic summary.
Task Description — the general topic for all tasks in the sequence.
Code Snippet — original or reference code (if provided during generation).
Distractor Indicator — a badge shows if distractor blocks are active for a task.
actions: 🧩 Solve Task — opens the student solver view (/solve/:id).
👩‍🏫 Review Task — opens the solver with teacher tools visible.
Share Sequence — copies a student-safe share link to clipboard.
✏️ Edit Task — modify the problem statement or code (teacher/owner only).
📤 Export — download this sequence as PDF (puzzle or free-form) or JSON/CSV.
Add to Worksheet — copy directly into one of your worksheets.
teacher: Automatically available for teachers and admins.
Expands solution accordions under each task card.
Shows distractor blocks alongside the model solution.
Allows switching to the teacher solver view with model solution overlay.
student: Only problem statements are shown — no model solutions.
Students click "Solve Task" to open the interactive solver.
sequence.editBody: If you own a sequence (or have copied it), you can edit any task's problem statement and code. The first save automatically preserves the original LLM-generated version for comparison and research purposes. You will be asked to rate the LLM output quality (1–5 stars) at first save.
edit: On foreign sequences, the Edit button is locked — copy the worksheet first.
sequence.similarBody: Teacher view shows a panel of sequences that share tags with this one, ranked by tag overlap and language match — a quick way to find related material without a fresh search. It hides itself when there's nothing similar.

solve.title: Solve Page Help
solve.intro: The Solve Page is where learners engage with Parsons problems — rearranging shuffled code blocks (and identifying distractor blocks) to reconstruct the correct program.
how: Blocks start shuffled in the "source" area. Move them to the "solution" area in the correct order.
Indent lines to create nested structures (drag-and-drop the indent handle, or use the indent buttons).
Press Check my solution to check correctness at any time.
Use Shuffle Lines to randomise again if you want a fresh start.
modes: Drag & Drop (default) — grab a block and drop it into position.

Click-to-Move — click a block to select it (it turns highlighted), then click the target slot to place it. Better for trackpads and tablets. Toggle in the toolbar; preference is saved across sessions.

Keyboard — Tab to move between blocks, arrow keys to reorder selected block. To indent a block via keyboard: select it, then use the + / − indent buttons in the block toolbar, or drag the indent handle on the left edge of the block.
Touch — long-press to select a block on mobile, tap to place it.
colors: 🟩 Green — correct line and indentation.
🟨 Yellow — indentation warning (non-critical, often still accepted).
🟥 Red — incorrect position or indentation.
solve.distractorBody: Some puzzles include distractor blocks — plausible-looking lines that do not belong in the correct solution. Distractor blocks look identical to real blocks; part of the challenge is identifying them and leaving them in the source area.
distractor: A distractor in your solution zone will always be marked red on Feedback.
Hints can help identify distractor blocks (they show up as a distinct hint type).
solve.interchangeableBody: Some tasks contain blocks that are equally valid in multiple positions — for example, two independent variable declarations, or two independent base cases in a recursive function. The grader recognises all valid permutations and marks them green.
solve.gapBody: Some blocks contain a small text input instead of being complete as-is — type the missing piece (a variable name, a value, an operator) directly into the gap. It's checked alongside block position and must be correct for the task to count as solved.
inlineSplit: Some blocks are split into several fragments you additionally arrange within the block — not just place the block as a whole.
A split can include distractor fragments too, styled the same as the real ones, on top of any whole-block distractors elsewhere in the puzzle.
Getting the fragment order wrong also blocks the "solved" verdict, just like a wrong gap answer.
solve.contextBody: Some tasks show a grey read-only block above and/or below the puzzle area. This is context code — the surrounding scaffold (e.g. a class definition, an import block, or a function that calls your result). You do not move these blocks; they are fixed. They exist to give you the full picture of where your solution fits. The grader ignores them — only the movable puzzle blocks are checked.
solve.hintsBody: When stuck, click the Hint 💡 button (only visible if hints are enabled for this worksheet):
hints: Level 1 (1 credit) — a static analysis tool (Ruff for Python, javac + SpotBugs for Java) analyses your current arrangement and highlights the problematic block(s) with a red pulsing border. A short message explains the type of error (e.g., "A block uses a variable that hasn't been defined yet").
Level 2 (2 credits) — click "Explain it to me" to get an LLM-generated explanation that references the highlighted blocks by label (A, B, …) and explains the logic in student-friendly language.
Hints disappear after you move a block — encouraging you to act, not just read.
If the worksheet sets a budget, the remaining credits are shown next to the buttons: 💡 3/5. Once they run out, both hint buttons are disabled.
solve.completionBody: When you solve the puzzle correctly:
completion: A "Solved correctly!" banner appears with your stats: attempts, time, hints used.
A short self-report (confidence rating) may appear — this is anonymous research data.
Use the "Next Task" button to advance to the next tier.
resume: Your arrangement is saved automatically as you work, a moment after each move — closing the tab, refreshing, or navigating away doesn't cost you your progress.
Reopening an unfinished task restores exactly where you left off, including indentation.
Once you've solved a task, that solved arrangement is what gets restored from then on — even if you click "Solve again" to try again and later abandon that attempt without re-solving it.
"Start over" is different: it appears only on unsolved work in progress and throws it away on purpose, dealing a fresh puzzle next time.
nav: ← Back to Sequence — returns to the sequence overview.
🔗 Share Task — copies a student-safe task link to clipboard.
teacherTools: Toggle Teacher Mode at the top right to show/hide the model solution panel.
The "Teacher Tools" box (bottom right) shows the model solution and distractor list.
Share button copies a student-facing version (without teacher mode enabled).
Block labels (A, B, …) in the model solution correspond to hint labels — useful for classroom discussion.
studentTips: Focus on logic, not syntax perfection — the grader understands minor indentation variations.
Use feedback iteratively; don't guess wildly. Try to understand each red block before moving on.
If a block keeps coming up red no matter where you put it, consider whether it might be a distractor.
Try Click-to-Move if drag-and-drop feels awkward on your device.
Use hints strategically — you have a limited credit budget per task.

hints.title: Hint System Help
hints.intro: The hint system provides structured, reliable help when a student is stuck. Unlike purely LLM-based hints, CodeOwl's hints are deterministic first: real static analysis tools run on the student's current block arrangement to identify concrete problems.
how: The student's current block arrangement is assembled into a complete code file.
A static analysis tool runs on that file.
Findings are mapped back to specific block IDs.
The affected blocks are highlighted with a red pulsing border.
A short pedagogical message describes the type of error — without giving the answer.
tools: Python → Ruff — ultra-fast Python linter. Key rules: F821 (undefined name — block used before definition), F841 (unused variable — block may be a distractor), E999 (syntax error), F811 (redefined name).
Java → javac (Stage 1) — compiler diagnostics catch undefined variables, type errors, and uninitialized variables.
Java → SpotBugs (Stage 2) — bytecode analysis for deeper bugs (null-pointer paths, dead stores, redundant null-checks). Only runs if the code compiles.
levelsRows: LLM explains the finding in student-friendly language
hints.levelsNote: Level 2 is not a diagnosis — the LLM receives the already-identified finding and only explains it. It does not analyse the code independently.
hints.distractorBody: If a distractor block is in the student's solution zone, the hint system detects this as the priority problem before running the full analysis:
distractor: Hint text: "One of the blocks in your workspace doesn't belong in the solution."
The distractor block is highlighted — but not explicitly named as a distractor.
edge: Too few blocks placed — if you have fewer blocks in the solution area than the correct answer requires, the hint tells you immediately: "Only X of Y required blocks have been placed. Drag the missing blocks into the solution area." This takes priority over all other findings so you don't get misleading analysis on an incomplete arrangement.
No findings — if the arrangement compiles/lints without errors but is still wrong, the fallback message is: "No static errors found. Check the order of your blocks."
Multiple findings — only the top 2 most severe findings are shown to avoid overwhelming the student.

Tool timeout / crash — the analysis tool is treated as having found nothing rather than failing loudly, so you silently get the same "No static errors found" fallback as a clean-but-wrong arrangement.
config: Enable Hints — checkbox. Off = Hint button hidden entirely.
Credits per task — 1–99, or unlimited (the default). Encourages strategic use over dependency.

distractors.title: Distractor System Help
distractors.intro: Distractor blocks are plausible-looking but incorrect code lines that are mixed into the puzzle block pool. The student must identify them and leave them in the source area. They test whether students genuinely understand the code — not just rearrangement.
taxonomyRows: Correct style, wrong variable used in expression
Wrong initial value or base case
Syntactically valid but contextually illegal (break outside loop)
generation: Plan — during sequence generation, the model chooses a distractor type and rationale per task (e.g., "LOGIC_FLIP: focus on Boolean inversion for early exits").
Solver pass — the correct solution is generated as normal.
Antagonist call — a separate LLM call ("CodeOwl Antagonist") generates the actual distractor lines, guided by the plan. Distractors end with #distractor internally.
distractors.generationNote: The solver and the antagonist are separate — the antagonist only sees the correct solution and the plan, not the solver's internal reasoning.
controls: Enable/Disable — toggle distractors per task or per sequence during/after generation.
Edit Distractors — open the Task Edit Modal → "Distractors" tab → edit, add, or remove distractor lines.
Regenerate — click "Regenerate Distractors" to get a fresh set from the antagonist.
The distractor plan (type + rationale) is shown for context so you know what the AI was trying to achieve.
tips: If a block stays red no matter where you place it, it may be a distractor.
Read each block carefully — distractors are designed to look plausible at a glance.
Hints can help: if a distractor is in your solution zone, the hint system specifically flags it.

teacher.title: Teacher Mode Help
teacher.intro: Teachers and admins automatically have access to Teacher Mode across all pages. Teacher Mode reveals model solutions, enables editing, and surfaces research tools.
toggle: Look for the yellow "Teacher View" button in the top-right of sequence and solve pages.
Students never see this button — teacher controls are gated by role, not just by URL.
sequence: Model solutions expand in accordion panels under each task card.
Distractor blocks are listed alongside the solution.
Edit, export, and copy buttons are visible.
Rating badge shows the LLM quality rating given when the task was first edited.
solve: "Teacher Tools" panel (bottom right) shows the model solution with block labels.
Share button generates a student-safe link (without teacher parameters).
Full hint functionality is available for testing even without a credit budget.
edit: Edit any task you own via the "Edit" button on the Sequence page.
The first save preserves the LLM original in the database for research comparison.
You rate the original LLM quality (1–5 stars) at first save — this becomes part of the research dataset.
All edits and their process (started / saved / cancelled) are logged as learning events for research.
teacher.dataBody: CodeOwl v2 logs structured learning events for research purposes (event-based, JSONB). This includes:
data: Task open/close times, feedback clicks, correct/abandoned events
Every individual block move (for strategy analysis)
Hint usage (level, timing, which blocks were highlighted)
Distractor interactions (placed, removed, time in workspace)
Teacher edit events (started, saved, duration, fields changed)
Self-report ratings (confidence, frustration — 1-click smileys after completion)
Session metadata (device type, viewport — once per session)
teacher.dataNote: No raw mouse tracking, no keystroke logging, no external tab tracking. Solving tasks via a shared link without logging in is possible — those events have user_id = null.
admin: User Management — view, edit, promote, and delete users.
Bulk Retag — re-run tag analysis across all sequences (useful after model updates or tag config changes).
Library Admin — merge duplicate tags, view newly discovered topics.

manualCreate.title: Manual Task Creator Help
manualCreate.intro: The Manual Task Creator lets you build a Parsons puzzle sequence without any LLM involvement — you write the problem statement and the correct code solution for each tier yourself. Use this when you want full control, or when you already have classroom code examples you want to turn into puzzles.
workflow: Set the programming language and concepts (comma-separated, e.g. for-loop, arrays).
For each tier (T1–T3), write a problem statement and paste the correct code solution.
Watch the live block preview on the right — it shows exactly how the code will be split into draggable blocks.
Click "Create sequence" to save. You're redirected to the new sequence page.
manualCreate.blocksBody: Every non-empty line in the solution editor becomes one block in the Parsons puzzle. Indentation in the code is automatically translated into indent levels — so a line indented by 4 spaces becomes a block at indent level 1, 8 spaces → level 2, etc.
blocks: Keep solutions focused — 5 to 12 non-empty lines is the sweet spot.
The line count and character count are shown below the editor.
<kbd>Tab</kbd> in the code editor inserts 4 spaces (no focus-trap).
tiers: Start with 1–3 tiers. Each tier is a separate puzzle at a different difficulty level.
Use the tab buttons at the top to switch between tiers — green badge ✓ means that tier has both a statement and a solution.
Use the Tier Level selector to assign T1 (easy), T2 (medium), or T3 (hard) to each slot.
You can add or remove tiers using the + / × buttons.
tips: After creation, you can still generate distractors via the sequence page.
The sequence is tagged automatically after creation — check the Library to verify tags.
Tiers don't have to share the same algorithm — T1 could be a simple loop, T3 a recursive version.

myClasses.title: My Classes Help (Students)
myClasses.intro: The My Classes page is your home screen as a student. It shows all the classes your teacher has enrolled you in, and from there you can access the worksheets assigned to your class.
nav: Open My Classes from the navigation bar.
Click a class card to open the class detail page.
You'll see the worksheets your teacher has assigned — click one to open it.
The worksheet lists all task sequences. Click "Solve Task" to start a puzzle.
faq: My class list is empty. — Ask your teacher to enrol you. You need to be added to a class before worksheets appear here.
I don't see a worksheet my teacher mentioned. — The teacher may not have assigned it to your class yet, or you may be in the wrong class.
Can I see tasks not assigned to my class? — Yes, if you have a direct link to a sequence or worksheet you can still view and solve it anonymously.
account: Your teacher created your account and gave you a one-time login link.
After logging in, you can set a personal password and email via your Profile.
Your progress (solved tasks, hints used) is saved to your account.

admin.title: Admin Panel Help
admin.intro: Admin tools give you global oversight of the CodeOwl platform — user accounts, tag hygiene, and bulk library operations. These pages are not visible to teachers or students.
users: View all users — list of every registered account with role, email, and creation date.
Edit role — promote a teacher to admin or demote back.
Delete user — removes the account. Sequences and worksheets owned by that user are preserved (owner_id is kept, but the user cannot log in).
Search / filter — filter by role or search by name/email.
library: Bulk Retag — re-runs the automatic tag analysis pipeline across all sequences (or just those missing an LLM tag). Runs as a background job with a live progress bar and a history of past runs. Use this after updating the tagger model or changing tag rules.

Bulk Concept Re-Classifier — the same kind of background job, but re-runs structural concept detection instead of tags (all sequences, or just those missing a concept). Separate from Bulk Retag because tags and concepts are independent systems.

New Topics Report — tags first seen within a configurable window (1–90 days), with usage counts and a one-click "Merge…" into an existing tag — the fastest way to catch a typo or near-duplicate before it spreads.
Merge Tags — combine duplicate or near-duplicate tags into one canonical form (e.g. for_loop + for-loop → for-loop). All sequence associations are updated automatically.
Tag Overview — see all tags sorted by usage count; spot orphaned or rarely-used tags that could be cleaned up.
database: Full backup — downloads a complete pg_dump of the database, restorable outside the app if ever needed.
Audit log — every backup and research-export download, who triggered it, when, its size and row count, and whether it succeeded.
research: Four datasets — learning events (every block move, hint and distractor interaction), feedback clicks, hint usage, and the students' saved arrangements. Switch with the tabs.

Filter by class — learning events and feedback clicks carry the class they happened in, so the filter is exact. Hints and submissions are matched through class membership and worksheet assignment instead.
Download CSV — exports exactly what the filters select, not just the visible page.
Download ZIP — all four datasets for the current class plus a _metadata.json recording which filters produced it.
Pseudonymous — rows carry UUIDs, never names or email addresses. Both downloads are recorded in the audit log on /admin/database.
caution: Bulk Retag overwrites existing auto-generated tags. Manual tags are never touched.
Merging tags is irreversible via the UI — make a DB backup before large merge operations.
Deleting users does not cascade-delete their content — verify you want to keep orphaned sequences.
